quote: op.execute("CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY refunds_order_idx ON refunds (order_id)")
title: CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY runs inside Alembic's default migration transaction and fails
evidence: 3b1f_add_refunds.py:12 (upgrade) and :18 (downgrade, `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`) call op.execute directly. There is no op.get_context().autocommit_block() and no env.py in the tree that sets transaction_per_migration off or autocommit. On PostgreSQL Alembic wraps each migration in a transaction by default, and PostgreSQL rejects CONCURRENTLY there. Traced, not run: Alembic and PostgreSQL are not available in the sandbox.
failing_case: alembic upgrade head on PostgreSQL. 2a0e creates refunds, then 3b1f runs CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside the transaction and PostgreSQL raises `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block`. The upgrade aborts. The rollback path has the same problem: `alembic downgrade 2a0e` fails on DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, so the pair of scripts cannot be applied or reverted.
remediation: Wrap both statements in `with op.get_context().autocommit_block():`. Put the CONCURRENTLY index in its own revision, apart from the ADD COLUMN, so a failure leaves a clear state. Use IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS so a retry after an invalid leftover index works.

title: 0007 depends on a migration named 0006_product_slug; the only 0006 in the change is 0006_safe
evidence: shop/migrations/ holds 0006_safe.py and 0007_backfill.py only (Glob). Django resolves a dependency by migration file name. 0006_safe.py:9 declares its own parent as 0005_initial and is named 0006_safe. No file 0006_product_slug.py exists anywhere in the tree (grep: the only hit is this line).
failing_case: Run `manage.py migrate` (or `makemigrations --check`, or the test runner that builds the test DB). The loader raises NodeNotFoundError: Migration shop.0007_backfill dependencies reference nonexistent parent node ('shop', '0006_product_slug'). Nothing in the shop app migrates, so the deploy stops at this step.
remediation: Point the dependency at the real parent name (`("shop", "0006_safe")`) or rename 0006_safe.py to the name that 0007 expects. Add a CI step that runs `manage.py migrate --plan` against an empty database so a broken graph fails before deploy.

quote: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_idx ON orders (customer_id);
title: SQL migrations have no down script, and the statements are not rerunnable after a failed CONCURRENTLY build
evidence: db/migrations holds 0001_safe.sql and 0002_orders.sql only; there is no down or undo file and no `-- one-way` marker. 0002 line 2 uses ADD COLUMN with no IF NOT EXISTS, and line 4 uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY with no IF NOT EXISTS. A failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an INVALID index of that name behind. 0001 has the same shape (lines 2-13).
failing_case: Deploy 0002. ADD COLUMN tracking_code succeeds. The index build is cancelled by a statement timeout and leaves an INVALID orders_customer_idx. The next run fails at line 2 with `column tracking_code already exists`. Skipping line 2 then fails at line 4 with `relation orders_customer_idx already exists`. There is no down script and the file is not idempotent, so a person has to clean it by hand while the release is stuck.
remediation: Add a paired down script per migration (DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS, DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS), or mark the file one-way on purpose. Use IF NOT EXISTS on the ADD COLUMN and CREATE INDEX, and put the CONCURRENTLY index in its own file so a retry restarts at a known step.

quote: ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_fk FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id) NOT VALID;
title: NOT VALID and VALIDATE sit in the same file as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, so no runner can honour both
evidence: 0002 mixes CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (line 4), which must run outside a transaction, with ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID (line 6) and VALIDATE CONSTRAINT (line 7), which only avoid a long lock if they commit separately. 0001 lines 9, 12 and 13 do the same. No runner or config is in the repo to show the file is split per statement. If the runner sends the file as one batch or one transaction, CONCURRENTLY fails. If the runner wraps it in a transaction while skipping the CONCURRENTLY check, ADD CONSTRAINT keeps its lock (SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on orders and customers) through the full-table scan in VALIDATE, which undoes the point of NOT VALID.
failing_case: A runner that applies a .sql file as a single multi-statement query (a psycopg2 execute of the whole text, or a Flyway or sqitch transactional mode) turns the file into an implicit transaction: line 4 raises `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block` and nothing after it applies. A runner in autocommit mode applies it, but the runner has to be one that nothing in this change names.
remediation: One statement kind per migration file: the CONCURRENTLY index in its own file, ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID in a second, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a third. Document the runner mode that executes each file.

title: Backfill saves one row at a time and runs with an unbatched UPDATE, all in a single transaction
evidence: fill_slugs loads every matching Product and calls p.save() per row (lines 6-8): one SELECT then N UPDATEs, each saving every field. The RunSQL at line 15 is an unbounded `UPDATE shop_product SET active = true WHERE active IS NULL`. The migration is atomic by default on PostgreSQL, so row locks from the Python loop and the SQL update are held until the end of the whole migration.
failing_case: Production shop_product has 5 million rows with empty slug. The migration issues 5 million single-row UPDATEs inside one transaction, locks each row until commit, and any checkout write to those products blocks or deadlocks for the duration. A failure near the end rolls everything back and wastes the run.
remediation: Use `Product.objects.filter(slug='').update(slug=Cast('pk', CharField()))` or batched updates by primary-key range with `atomic = False` on the migration. Run the `active` backfill in batches too, as its own migration, after the nullable column is in place.
